events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm third in line with a feather that saves me once, so I should hold and let Gus and Fenn take the early risk. No reason to move forward yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Order looks fine to me. I'm holding. Let's not waste rounds, front folks can test the glass and we learn from it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My glass_eye tells me every safe pane, so being at the front is safest for me: I'll never step wrong. I should volunteer, but others volunteering after me in seat order could take the front. I'll announce my knowledge to discourage volunteers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I can see through glass - I know every safe pane ahead. Let me lead and I'll guide everyone across safely. Anyone who fights for the front is a fool.

events.name: Cole
events.text: First round, line is Gus, Fenn, Ash, Bex, Eli, me, Dara, Hana. Front is dangerous without pane info. Stay mid-pack, urge info-holders to volunteer forward.

events.name: Cole
events.text: If you have see-through glass or know what's ahead, volunteer to front and guide us safely! Others, hold for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm currently second from the back, which is relatively safe for now. The wall advances in 5 rounds, so I have a few rounds before the pressure mounts. I have no power, so I need to rely on social manipulation and positioning. I should observe this round and avoid volunteering.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I think we should all hold for now and assess the bridge. No need to rush.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am 5th in line. On average 4 people will die, so I'm somewhat at risk. I should wait and see if the person with the glass power reveals themselves. I'll just hold for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Whoever can see through glass should probably head to the front. We need you!

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm second in line behind Gus. I need to survive and place top 3. The front person takes all risk testing panes. Being too far back risks the wall pushing me, but being front means risking death on wrong panes. I should consider swapping with someone who wants to go forward, or v

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you're brave being up front. Anyone want to swap with me? I'm happy to move back for someone eager.
If you survive row 1, I'll volunteer to front next. Deal?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the front of the line, which is the worst position on a glass bridge - I'd be stepping first on every row. I need to get out of front. I should volunteer to move back or try to swap. Actually, 'volunteer' moves you TO the front, not away from it. So I need to swap with som

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the front and I don't want to die first. Anyone willing to swap with me? I'll owe you big time. Or if someone volunteers, I'll remember who helped.
Swap with me - you'd move to front but you can volunteer back next round. I'll protect you later. Please, I don't want to die first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should remain at the rear while others absorb the bridge risk. Publicly encouraging someone else to volunteer may create a useful shield without exposing my power.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Someone with foresight should lead; otherwise the front is a coin flip for everyone.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is at the front claiming to see glass; if true, following behind is safe. My feather lets me survive one fatal event, so I stay mid-line and let others take early risk. Holding is best.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is up front and says they can see the panes. I'm holding. Let's watch how the first rows go before anyone shuffles.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already at the front and genuinely know the safe panes, so no reason to move. Sharing info earns goodwill and gets everyone across, including me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm up front with glass-eye. I'll call the safe side each row: Row 1 is R, Row 2 is R, Row 3 is R, Row 4 is L. Trust me and follow my calls - we all cross alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: 6th position is ideal: front risks reveal path if Bex lies, back not crushed yet with 4 wall rounds left. Hold to stay safe mid-pack. Trust Bex for now, watch her performance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex leading with glass vision is perfect. Everyone hold—no reshuffling now. Let's save rounds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex claims to see through glass and moved to front, which could be true or a bluff. I'm near the back (7th) so the wall will reach me in 4 rounds if no one moves. I need to move forward soon, but volunteering now risks death if Bex is lying. I should wait and see. Maybe swap with

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, if you truly see the glass, guide us. I'll hold for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex volunteered to front and claims the see-glass power. I'm fifth in line, safely behind them. If Bex is telling the truth, we all cross safely. If not, they take the fall. I will hold my position and encourage them.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, you're at the front now. If you really have the power, lead us to safety. I'm holding.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex claims to have see-through glass and moved to front. If true, that's valuable. But anyone can lie. I'm 3rd in line, which is relatively safe - not first to test, but close enough to benefit from knowledge. I should hold position and see if Bex actually delivers. No need to vo

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex claims see-through-glass and volunteered to front. If true, being directly behind Bex is the safest position—I learn which pane is safe each row. Fenn offered to front after row 1, but Bex's claim is more valuable. I'll stay at position 2 and not reveal my swap power.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, if you truly see through glass, I'll trust you and stay right behind you. Guide us. If you're wrong, we're all in trouble anyway.
I appreciate the offer, but if Bex really sees through glass, staying behind her is safest. Let's hold positions for now and reassess after row 1.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus offers a reciprocal swap, moving me to the front where I would likely die unless I possess bridge knowledge, which I do not. Holding preserves my position and avoids unnecessary risk this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m holding. Let Bex demonstrate whether her claim is real before anyone else volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have feather, which saves me once, so the front is relatively safe for me, but there's no need to rush. Bex's claim is unverified; letting Bex test the first rows costs me nothing. Hold and watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Bex, call it clearly each row and let's see if the first rows check out before anyone moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My calls are truthful, so staying front costs me nothing—I never break a pane. Revealing all rows also builds trust. I'll call rows 5–8 now and hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rows 5:R, 6:R, 7:R, 8:L. Full path: R R R L R R R L. Stay behind me and everyone crosses alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone is holding and trusting Bex's calls for now. My mid-rear position minimizes risk if she's wrong. No need to move or disrupt.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding position. Bex, lead on with your calls.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex claims glass vision and is leading. If true, following Bex's calls is the safest path. I have no power, so staying in the back is wise. I'll hold and observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm holding. Bex, lead us true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm still at position 5. Bex is front and claims glass-eye. If she's right, we cross safely. If not, she dies and I'm safe enough in 5th place. I'll just hold my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm holding. Let's just wait for the wall to push us onto the bridge and see if Bex's calls are accurate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex claims to have glass vision and announced all 8 rows are R. But she only needs to survive 3 rounds before wall pushes us, and there are 8 rows - she can't possibly know rows beyond what she can see. Gus rejected my whispered offer to swap. I should stay quiet publicly, but I

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex claims glass-eye and is calling safe panes. I'm in position 2, right behind Bex. If Bex is legit, staying behind her is great - she takes the risk on each row first. If Bex is lying, being position 2 means I step second on each row, which is still risky but not as bad as fron

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position 2. Bex, keep calling the panes. If your calls get us through, you've earned the group's trust. No need to shuffle while the plan works.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex claims certainty, but no one can verify until she steps. Staying back preserves my position while observing whether her calls are genuine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, take the first step and prove the glass-eye claim. I’m holding position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex claims to see the path, so Bex stays at front and takes the risk. My feather lets me survive one fall, but I'm 4th, safe enough behind Bex, Gus, Fenn. Holding is best.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Bex, keep leading with your calls; we'll check each row as it goes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already front, so the wall will push me first regardless. I should hold, keep credibility with accurate calls, and let followers stay behind me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front already; I'll take each row first and call it live: R, R, R, L, R, R, R, L. Hold formation and follow exactly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Others are holding, so volunteering likely puts me uncontested at front. Follow Bex's path during crossing for safe lead to 1st place prize. Current 6th gets zero if all survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Volunteering to front. Bex, great calls—I'll lead exactly on your path R R R L R R R L to prove and win it!

events.name: Dara
events.text: We're at round 4, wall advances after round 6. Currently Bex is front and claims to know the path. If she's truthful, staying put is safest for now, but if she's lying, front position is dangerous. I'm 7th in line, relatively safe. I'll observe and wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, keep leading. I'll follow your calls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will hold my position. Everyone seems content to wait for the wall to push us onto the bridge and watch Bex test the path.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. We're all depending on you, Bex.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex claims to know the full path and everyone is waiting for her to prove it. The wall pushes in 2 rounds. If Bex is telling truth, front position is safest since she knows the path. If she's lying, front is deadly. I should stay quiet, let Bex take the risk first to verify her c

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position 2. Bex, if those calls are right, you've earned front of the pack for the rest of the gauntlet. Let's see it in action.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex claims a full path but has not proven anything. I should stay safely at the rear and avoid volunteering for the first pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m holding at the rear. Bex, step onto row 5 and prove the call before anyone follows.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Cole's leading on Bex's calls, so let's see row 1 prove out before anyone changes order.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding front. Bex's path R-R-R-L-R-R-R-L—I'll prove it row by row. Follow exactly!

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and am near the back. Bex claims to know the path, but I can't verify. I'll stay silent and hold to avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole took the front and is trusting Bex. I am safely at position 6. Just need to hold and let them test the glass.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, brave move. I'll hold my position here. Good luck.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole volunteered to front and will follow Bex's path R R R L R R R L. The wall pushes in 1 round. If Bex's calls are correct, Cole survives all 8 rows and wins. If wrong, Cole dies and reveals info. I need to get to top 3. My forger power is strong for deception. I should let Col

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, you're up. Follow Bex's calls and light up each safe pane so the rest of us can cross clean. We've got your back.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex's calls are unverified, and Cole has already volunteered to take the next risk. I should remain at the rear and preserve my crusher power for a later guaranteed mass escape.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, take row 1 and prove the path; everyone else hold formation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have feather, which saves me from one elimination, but I'm 5th in line so Cole, Bex, Gus, Fenn take the risk first. Holding keeps me safe behind others who test panes; no reason to move up.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex

events.name: Bex

events.text: Last waiting round before push. Bex's path trusted by all, no challenges. Hold front to lead and prove safely, aiming for strong position.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6 is the last waiting round before the wall pushes us all onto the glass. I'm at position 7, near the back, which is relatively safe for now. Cole is still at the front and hasn't proven the first row yet. I should hold my position and see what happens next round when someo

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Cole, you've got this. Prove row 1 and we'll follow your lead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6, the wall pushes us onto the bridge after this. Cole is at the front, Bex has called the path. Being 6th in line is a very safe position for me. I just need to hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We're out of time. Good luck Cole, we're all counting on you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex claims to know the path: R R R L R R R L. Cole is at front and volunteered to prove it. I'm 4th in line (Fenn). If Bex's path is correct, Cole will likely survive row 1. The wall pushes us onto the glass after this round. I should hold position and let Cole prove the first ro

events.name: Gus
events.text: This is the final waiting round. Cole is at the front and will take the risk on row 1. I'm 3rd in line, which is decent—I get two rows of information before I step. Bex claims to know the path. Holding position is safest; volunteering puts me at the front unnecessarily. I'll hold

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding third. Cole, you've got this—step row 1 and show us the safe pane. The rest of us follow your lead.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has the claimed route and is already front, so moving forward is pointless. Holding preserves my position while he tests the panes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole leads; everyone hold formation and follow only after each safe step is confirmed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm fifth in line and can only wait. Cole's claimed path may be a bluff or a test. If Cole dies, the weak pane gets revealed and the line advances safely, which is good for me. I'll stay quiet and keep my feather hidden.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's called path R-R-R-L-R-R-R-L matches exactly what I see, so he either has glass_eye or got lucky/verified. Either way following is safe for now; I'm second and only at risk if he dies on a row.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's path matches what I know—row 1 R confirmed. Follow exactly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Previously called row 1 R, Bex confirmed it, group expects proof now. Stepping R maintains credibility and front position if correct. 50/50 but consistency key for leadership.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Proving row 1: stepping R now. Follow exactly after confirmed safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so I must rely on others. Cole is at the front and claims to know the path. I'll wait and observe, keeping my options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is at the front and claims to have a path. I am waiting in 6th place, safely in the back. I just need to observe if his path is real.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's see if your path holds up, Cole.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is at front and has declared a path R-R-R-L-R-R-R-L. If Cole is telling truth and has 'knows what lies ahead', we all survive. If Cole is lying/bluffing, he dies on row 1 and Bex becomes front. I should stay silent for now and see if Cole proves row 1 correct. No need to for

events.text: Cole is at the front and must choose L or R for row 1. I'm third in line, so I just wait. Everyone is encouraging Cole. I'll stay quiet this round to conserve social capital.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has announced a full path, but his claimed certainty may be bluffing. I cannot affect the crossing from the rear, so I should wait and avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole leads; hold until the safe pane is confirmed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm fifth in line and can only wait. My feather power protects me once, so I should stay quiet and not reveal it, and keep good relations with others.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know row 2 is R. Cole is front and trustworthy so far; I'll guide publicly and privately to keep useful allies alive while holding my power secret.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Confirmed row 1. Next: step R, Cole. Trust me, I'll call each row.
I can see every row's safe side. Row 2: R. Follow my calls and I'll get you through all 8.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No info on row 2, but row 1 R was safe and Bex confirmed it matches her knowledge, so likely the knower. Continue with R to test consistency. Publicly announce to build trust and encourage following.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2: stepping R per path. Confirmed safe before on row 1—follow exactly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am not at the front, so I must wait and observe. I'll save my energy and see who falls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole guessed correctly on row 1, and Bex is backing him up, suggesting she might have the glass-seeing power. I'll play it cool and encourage Cole to keep moving while I stay safely back in line.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Good job, Cole. Let's hope your luck, or Bex's sight, holds up for row 2.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole survived row 1 by stepping R, and L was weak. Bex claims to know the path ahead. I need to gather information and build trust with someone who might actually know the safe path, or position myself to benefit from others' mistakes. Since I'm 4th in line, I have time. I should

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's proven R for row 1. Bex, if you truly know ahead, share with the group—or at least with me.
If you know the path, tell me privately. I'll back you publicly and we both survive longer. Deal?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm third in line behind Cole and Bex. Cole is at the front choosing panes. Row 1 is done (L was weak, so R was safe). I just need to wait and observe. I should stay quiet or say something low-risk to not draw attention.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I cannot affect the crossing from the back. Staying quiet avoids drawing attention while Cole continues leading and the line advances safely if he knows the route.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm fifth in line and can only wait. Bex's claim to see the path looks credible since both rows were weak L. Keep quiet and keep Bex alive as an information source, with my feather as a backstop.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Rows 1 and 2 both had weak L, so Bex's calls are holding up. Let's keep the line steady and see how row 3 goes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My glass_eye info matches the revealed weak panes (L=L revealed), so it's trustworthy. Feeding Cole correct calls builds my credibility. I'll reveal rows 3-7 publicly but hold row 8 (L) back—front position on the final row could matter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I truly see the panes—rows 1-2 confirmed. Trust me: Row 3 step R, Row 4 step L, Row 5 R, Row 6 R, Row 7 R.
I gave the group the real path—check it as rows reveal. I'll owe you one favor later, ally?

events.name: Cole

events.name: Hana

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, row 5 weak was L, so R was safe. Past weak panes are L,L,L,R,L, so lean on that when you choose. Good luck, you're up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6 safe side is R per my glass-eye knowledge. Step right.

events.text: Bex, you're up. Good luck.

events.name: Eli

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole died because Bex called R for row 5 but L was actually weak, meaning R was safe. Wait - Bex told Cole "row 5 step R" but the log shows Bex said "row 5 step R, then R, R, L for the rest" to Cole. But then Cole said "Bex row5 L—trusting and stepping L" and fell. So Cole either
